html:
The Yuin are a group of Aboriginal Australian peoples of the South Coast of New South Wales, between the mountains and the sea. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

All Yuin share ancestors who spoke the Yuin language dialects, and they are made up of several groups, among them the Walbunja, Djiringanj and Wandandian. Their country runs from forested ranges down to estuaries and beaches, rich in fish and shellfish. Mount Gulaga is their most sacred mountain.

At Twofold Bay on the far south coast, Yuin people hunted whales with the help of killer whales, which drove baleen whales into the bay; European whalers later took up the same partnership in the 1800s. Neighbours included the Tharawal to the north, the Gundungurra and Ngunawal inland, and the Bidhawal to the south. Settlers and timber getters moved into Yuin land from the 1820s and 1830s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Yuin are a group of Aboriginal Australian peoples of the South Coast of New South Wales, between the mountains and the sea. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.
